title: Work as a cement finisher and mechanic
summary: He describes his trade as cement finishing, learned from Bo Brothers after the service in 1945, plus carpentry and truck repair.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. I remember we were, yeah, no, we were just walking to the bar. We were just walking to the hall and you walked by and handed you the paper. Well then, uh, seeing, what are you doing now for a living? I mean... Me? Yeah, I mean, you do, you do a lot of carpentry and...
I was human finishing.
That's what your profession is. That's my profession.
That's my profession.
When did you learn that?
I learned that from working with Bo Brothers.
Oh, when did you go to work for Bo Brothers? After I came on the service.
I know. Forty-five.
Oh, no. I know. I used to take pictures of all that stuff they were doing when they were making those overpasses and underpasses. Yeah. And you learned that on the job, like on the job training?
I learned that on the job. And then I did all that job then I worked for myself.
And you still have your own business?
My own business. I worked for me.
Well, you do other things too, don't you? You do carpentry.
I don't do no painting. I do carpentry work.
You do carpentry work? What else?
Mechanic work.
I let the mother go out.
Most of your mechanic work is done on your truck, fixing it, huh?
T-79. Don't leave me, my lady.
Don't leave me.

Yeah, but that's one thing I'm about to say. When he's drinking, he doesn't drive that truck. He leaves it right there. Remember the night you were too high and you did take the truck and you ran in the back of a taxi?
That's right. He didn't have to work.
